text.p: Lehman Brothers said on Thursday it initiated coverage of Spain's leading home pizza company Grupo Telepizza SA and rated it a "buy".
Telepizza, which controls nearly 70 percent of Spain's fast food market, was best positioned in the fast growing market where pizza was a clear favourite, Lehman said in research note.
From 1997 to 2000, sales would rise by an average of 40 percent while profits would rise by 37 percent, Lehman said.
Despite Telepizza's aggressive expansion it would continue to return good profits to its shareholders, it said. Earnings per share would rise to 231 Spanish pesetas from 159 pesetas.

Telepizza reported sales of 5.69 billion pesetas and a net profit of 0.48 billion pesetas in the first quarter of the current financial year. In 1996 it posted a net profit of 1.7 billion pesetas on sales of 19.36 billion pesetas.
